description_block: This 2026 All-Star basketball was used during the NBA All-Star Championship Game on February 15, 2026, when Team USA Stars faced Team Stripes in the final matchup of the NBA's reimagined All-Star tournament. The championship showcased some of the league's brightest talents, with Anthony Edwards and Chet Holmgren each scoring 8 points, while Tyrese Maxey led Team USA Stars with 9 points. On the opposing side, LeBron James contributed 5 points in what marked his historic and record-breaking 22nd NBA All-Star Game appearance, further extending one of the most remarkable legacies in the history of professional basketball. Anthony Edwards earned All-Star Game MVP honors, leading Team USA Stars to a commanding 47-21 victory and cementing his place among the league's premier young superstars. Beyond the final score, this game represented a symbolic passing of the torch between generations of NBA greatness. It served as the culmination of a hard-fought and highly anticipated All-Star tournament that brought together some of basketball's most accomplished veterans and its emerging future stars. Team Stripes featured an extraordinary collection of established NBA legends and All-Star veterans, including LeBron James, Kevin Durant, Jalen Brunson, Kawhi Leonard, Jaylen Brown, Donovan Mitchell, and De’Aaron Fox. Collectively, this group represented countless All-Star appearances, championships, MVP awards, and some of the defining moments of the modern NBA era. Standing opposite them was a fearless and talented group of young stars eager to establish themselves as the league's next generation of elite players. Led by Anthony Edwards, the roster featured Cade Cunningham, Tyrese Maxey, Devin Booker, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Duren, Scottie Barnes, and Jalen Johnson. Their dominant performance throughout the tournament and in the championship game highlighted the changing landscape of the NBA and demonstrated the depth of young talent poised to carry the league into its next chapter. The 2026 NBA All-Star Championship Game will be remembered as a historic showcase of basketball excellence, bringing together future Hall of Famers, current superstars, and rising phenoms on one stage. This basketball features the official Los Angeles All-Star logo, created for the league’s 75th All-Star Game. It also commemorates the occasion with “75th Annual” detailing and star markings that highlight each prior year the game has been held in Los Angeles. This ball has been photomatched by PSA Photomatching.
title: 2026 NBA All-Star Championship Game Used Basketball | Game 4 | Team Stars vs. Team Stripes

In the 2013-2014 campaign, Randle averaged a double-double, with 15 points and 10.4 rebounds per game while helping Kentucky reach the National Championship Game. Randle led the Knicks to their first playoff appearance in eight seasons in 2020-2021, was named an All-Star as well as Most Improved Player, and was named to the All-NBA Second Team. After teaming up with Jalen Brunson, Randle was again named an All-Star in 2023 and earned a place on the All-NBA 3rd Team. He and Brunson led the Knicks to their first playoff win in a decade when the Knicks beat the Cleveland Cavaliers. Before the 2024-25 season, Randle was traded to the Timberwolves as part of a blockbuster deal that sent Karl-Anthony Towns to the Knicks. Randle was then dealt in the summer of 2026 to the Brooklyn Nets, as part of a larger deal that sent Naz Reid to the Charlotte Hornets, and LaMelo Ball to the Timberwolves.  At the time of cataloging, Randle has career averages of 19.2 points, 8.9 rebounds, and 3.9 assists per game.
